learningObjective: Explain what a Grouped GEMM is and why it is preferred over per-expert independent GEMMs in sparse MoE serving.
stem: In a sparse MoE layer with E experts, after routing each expert i receives n_i tokens (n_i variable, sum n_i = k * B * N). Which choice best describes Grouped GEMM and why it is used?

options.text: Grouped GEMM executes E GEMMs of shapes [n_i, D] x [D, F] as a single kernel launch that dispatches per-group tile schedules across SMs. Compared to E independent GEMM launches, it amortizes launch overhead and lets small n_i groups share SMs with larger groups, avoiding SM under-utilization on skinny GEMMs.

Grouped GEMM sums the outputs of E GEMMs into a single [B*N, F] tensor as part of the same kernel; the 'grouping' refers to the reduction across experts, and the kernel is chosen because it fuses the final combination step of MoE.

Grouped GEMM pads all n_i to the same length n_max and runs a single batched GEMM [E, n_max, F]. It is preferred because a single batched GEMM primitive is always faster than a grouped kernel; the padding overhead is negligible.

Grouped GEMM is a Winograd-like transform that combines groups of adjacent experts into a shared linear operator; only the transform + inverse-transform cost per group scales with n_i, so the algorithm reduces FLOPs by a factor of E.

explanation: Grouped GEMM (as in CUTLASS/cuBLAS grouped-GEMM APIs) fuses many independent GEMMs of varying shapes into a single kernel launch. It computes a per-group tile schedule so that SMs can work on tiles from any group in parallel, avoiding the SM-underutilization problem that occurs if you dispatch each expert's small GEMM independently. This is critical for MoE where token counts per expert (n_i) are small and highly variable. Padding to n_max would waste flops proportional to expert imbalance; grouped GEMM avoids that waste.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: standard rationale for MoE grouped GEMM.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: grouping is over independent GEMM problems, not over an output-summation reduction.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: padding wastes compute proportional to imbalance; grouped GEMM avoids padding.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: fabricates a Winograd-like decomposition; grouped GEMM does not reduce FLOPs.

assumptions: Token distribution across experts is variable and often skewed.
Modern CUTLASS or cuBLAS grouped-GEMM APIs are available.
nonImplications: Does not imply grouped GEMM is faster than batched GEMM for uniformly-sized groups; batched is fine there.
Does not imply zero routing overhead; the permutation of tokens into per-expert input buffers still costs a scatter kernel.

distractorRationales.B: Confuses group over problem shapes with reduction across outputs.

sourceRefs.locator: CUTLASS grouped GEMM for irregular problem sizes

performanceClaim.scope: Grouped GEMM utility for MoE with variable per-expert token counts
